title: Azure Static Web Apps Overview
description: Host single-page applications and static sites with a built-in API, authentication, and GitHub-based deployment.

data.text: Azure Static Web Apps (SWA) hosts a static front end and an optional serverless API as one unit. It serves the front end from a global content network, proxies `/api/*` requests to a managed Azure Functions instance, and provides built-in authentication so you do not have to write a login flow. It is designed for single-page applications, documentation sites, and JAMstack front ends.

data.caption: The static front end is served globally; /api routes are proxied to managed Functions; authentication is handled by the platform.
data.definition:
flowchart TD
    USER["Browser"] --> CDN["Global static content"]
    USER -->|/api/*| API["Managed Functions API"]
    USER -->|/.auth/*| AUTH["Built-in authentication"]
    AUTH --> IDP["Microsoft Entra ID,\nGitHub, Google"]
    CDN --> SPA["SPA assets\nHTML, JS, CSS"]
    API --> DB["Database or service"]

data.text: A `staticwebapp.config.json` file controls routing, access rules, and fallback behavior. Protected routes use roles, and the platform exposes the signed-in user at `/.auth/me`.

data.title: Route and authorization rules
data.content: Unmatched client-side routes fall back to index.html so a SPA router works, while API and asset paths are excluded from the fallback. Unauthenticated requests to protected routes are redirected to the identity provider.

data.title: GitHub Actions workflow
data.content: Creating the Static Web App with `--login-with-github` adds the deployment token as a repository secret and commits this workflow.
data.code:
name: Deploy static web app

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]

jobs:
  build-and-deploy:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    name: Build and deploy
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Build and deploy
        uses: Azure/static-web-apps-deploy@v1
        with:
          azure_static_web_apps_api_token: ${{ secrets.AZURE_STATIC_WEB_APPS_API_TOKEN }}
          repo_token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          action: upload
          app_location: "/"
          api_location: "api"
          output_location: "dist"

data.title: Create the Static Web App with the CLI
data.content: The command links the repository; each push to the branch triggers a deployment.
data.code:
az staticwebapp create \
  --name swa-demo \
  --resource-group rg-demo \
  --source https://github.com/myorg/myrepo \
  --location westeurope \
  --branch main \
  --app-location "/" \
  --api-location "api" \
  --output-location "dist" \
  --login-with-github

data.title: When Static Web Apps is not enough
data.text: SWA is optimized for static front ends plus a small API. If you need server-side rendering with full Node or .NET control, background processing, websockets, or a database connection pool, use App Service or Container Apps instead. SWA's managed Functions are convenient but have limits on runtime, scaling, and configuration.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Static Web Apps hosts a static front end and an optional managed Functions API as one resource.
The front end is served from a global content network; /api/* requests are proxied to the API.
staticwebapp.config.json controls routes, roles, fallbacks, and auth redirects.
Built-in authentication supports Microsoft Entra ID, GitHub, and Google; the user is available at /.auth/me.
GitHub Actions deploys the app on every push using the deployment token.
Use App Service or Container Apps when you need full server-side control.
